meaning: Proposed implementation backlog. None of these end-state acceptance criteria is claimed satisfied by merely listing it.

priorities.P0: Required for the relevant safety/first-boot/promotion milestone
priorities.P1: Required for a dependable managed service
priorities.P2: Scale, optional integration or product scope; not required for an offline first guest

milestones.B: One genuinely bootable, semantically tested guest

items.implementation_gap: Define operator, cargo author, guest, engine, hull and host trust boundaries. Keep control-plane permission, guest capability and proof status as separate fields.
items.acceptance_test: A reviewed threat model maps every entry point to its actual enforcement boundary; no declaration is labeled enforcement.

items.implementation_gap: Specify boot, invoke, stop, inspect, snapshot and error contracts with strict required fields, extensions and version negotiation.
items.acceptance_test: Contract tests reject unknown incompatible versions, duplicate fields and unsupported capabilities before mutation.

items.implementation_gap: Separate desired and observed states: admitted, staged, built, booting, ready, running, draining, stopped, failed and quarantined.
items.acceptance_test: Every transition has a durable reason and legal predecessor; failed readiness cannot produce a running status.

items.implementation_gap: Extend checksum parsing to duplicate-key-safe JSON, schema migration, canonical encoding and non-ambiguous field semantics.
items.acceptance_test: Equivalent manifests hash consistently; malicious duplicates and lossy downgrade migrations are rejected.

items.implementation_gap: Use immutable workload IDs and monotonic generations rather than directory names as authority across replacement and restore.
items.acceptance_test: A stale process cannot write state or publish results for a replacement with the same display name.

items.implementation_gap: Define which files are input, generated, excluded or runtime state; preserve an explicit rejection/exclusion ledger for every ingest.
items.acceptance_test: Every original archive member is either hash-accounted cargo or has a documented policy disposition; no silently lost dependencies.

items.implementation_gap: Distinguish sorting, metadata witnessing, dialect compilation and actual application execution. Define supported source languages and observable semantics.
items.acceptance_test: A nontrivial application passes semantic input/output tests on its target; a row-sequence hash alone never satisfies execution.

items.implementation_gap: Represent source, compiler, runtime, configuration, guest image, state schema and evidence as a typed acyclic graph.
items.acceptance_test: Changing any dependency invalidates exactly the affected images/evidence; cycles and missing dependencies are rejected.

items.implementation_gap: Choose one initial target such as a selected Unikraft configuration or a Solo5-compatible library OS. Port one supported C engine/workload first, not all runtimes at once.
items.acceptance_test: A clean build links the application and only required OS libraries into a guest image, not a host Python command.

items.implementation_gap: Implement the selected architecture entry point, boot information validation, stack setup and platform startup sequence.
items.acceptance_test: The chosen VMM loads the image and reaches a guest-originated ready signal without a conventional guest OS boot.

items.implementation_gap: Define executable sections, relocations, memory map, zero initialization, overflow bounds and supported image format.
items.acceptance_test: Malformed images are rejected; executable and writable regions follow the selected platform protection policy.

items.implementation_gap: Provide bounded allocation, failure behavior, stack budgets and memory ownership appropriate to the linked runtime.
items.acceptance_test: Memory exhaustion yields a documented failure without host escape or cross-guest corruption.

items.implementation_gap: Select cooperative, preemptive or run-to-completion semantics; implement required timers, interrupt handling and cancellation points.
items.acceptance_test: A deliberately non-terminating workload can be stopped at the host boundary and cannot starve other guests.

items.implementation_gap: Keep deterministic simulation time separate from real monotonic time and cryptographic randomness; validate boot-time availability.
items.acceptance_test: Replay uses recorded inputs while security keys never derive from deterministic witness seeds or replay clocks.

items.component: Minimal console, block and transport drivers
items.implementation_gap: Implement only devices needed by the first workload: bounded console, selected block device and optional transport with validated descriptors.
items.acceptance_test: Malformed descriptors and unavailable devices fail safely; no unused device is exposed by default.

items.component: Guest ABI conformance and panic reporting
items.implementation_gap: Build positive/negative ABI probes, panic records and source-mapped traces for the chosen image/runtime combination.
items.acceptance_test: A boot-success artifact includes image digest, ABI version, workload output and intentionally induced panic evidence.

items.implementation_gap: Separate host-process adapters from actual guest backends; expose explicit isolation classes and capability negotiation.
items.acceptance_test: An isolation-required workload cannot silently fall back to an in-process or ordinary subprocess adapter.

items.implementation_gap: Implement one supported backend that creates a separate guest instance from the built image and validates its boot configuration.
items.acceptance_test: Two guest instances are independently booted, inspected and stopped; host-only VM interpreter runs cannot pass this gate.

items.implementation_gap: Constrain the VMM/tender with the selected OS mechanisms: user identity, syscall policy, filesystem access and process isolation.
items.acceptance_test: An adversarial guest cannot access unrelated host files or make forbidden host operations through exposed devices.

items.implementation_gap: Translate NETWORK=deny into absent devices and/or enforced host filtering. Explicitly isolate the host control-plane and metadata endpoints.
items.acceptance_test: A guest traffic probe demonstrates denied egress and lateral access; policy text alone is not evidence.

items.component: CPU, memory, I/O and process quotas
items.implementation_gap: Apply aggregate per-workload and per-tenant limits, including compiler children, decoder workers and inherited processes.
items.acceptance_test: Memory, fork, log and I/O flood probes remain inside quota and preserve another guest's health.

items.implementation_gap: Track each child by generation, enforce deadlines, bound stdout/stderr, kill the complete tree and reap zombies.
items.acceptance_test: Timeout and parent crash leave no executable orphan; failure reason and last bounded log survive.

items.implementation_gap: Concentrate privileged device/network operations in a small authenticated broker instead of the entire ship process.
items.acceptance_test: Unprivileged ship operation succeeds with only narrowly scoped broker requests; arbitrary paths and commands are denied.

items.implementation_gap: Expand doctor from informational checks to exercised backend capability probes, patch policy and immutable run-time evidence.
items.acceptance_test: Admission records the selected backend and verified constraints; unavailable virtualization blocks rather than degrades security.

items.implementation_gap: Pin compiler, linker, libraries, engine sources and runtime artifacts with offline-usable checksums and origins.
items.acceptance_test: Build works from an explicit dependency cache without implicit PATH/download substitutions; missing inputs are refused.

items.implementation_gap: Normalize timestamps, environment, source paths and generated metadata while separating nondeterministic build evidence.
items.acceptance_test: Two isolated clean builders produce matching declared image digests or a precisely documented reproducibility boundary.

items.implementation_gap: Treat compilers, build hooks and imported project tooling as untrusted execution with disposable roots and quotas.
items.acceptance_test: A hostile build cannot read operator secrets, contact unapproved endpoints or persist outside its workspace.

items.implementation_gap: Compare source semantics, intermediate representation and native results across supported dialects; bound lowering sizes and arithmetic.
items.acceptance_test: Generated and hand-written semantic test programs agree under edge cases; unsupported features are refused explicitly.

items.implementation_gap: Address images and dependency blobs by digest, verify reads, publish atomically and separate source from executable outputs.
items.acceptance_test: Interrupted publication exposes no partial image; a modified blob is rejected even when its filename matches.

items.component: Software bill of materials and license inventory
items.implementation_gap: Produce machine-readable component/version/source/license records for the guest, host, bundled hull and hold.
items.acceptance_test: Every linked or shipped runtime dependency maps to a source/version/license and a reviewable provenance record.

items.implementation_gap: Bind image digest to inputs, build recipe, builder identity and observed tests; use SLSA concepts without claiming an unassessed level.
items.acceptance_test: An independent verifier reconstructs the build relationship and rejects altered subjects or unknown builders.

items.implementation_gap: Verify release signatures against operator-established trust roots before build, mount or execution; disable implicit trust enrollment for untrusted cargo.
items.acceptance_test: An intact but self-signed or unapproved image is rejected; signature policy failure never becomes a checksum-only pass.

items.implementation_gap: Convert declared entry points and dependency edges into actual invocations, not merely script placement into folders.
items.acceptance_test: A multi-step workload executes dependencies exactly in the required order and publishes explicit outputs.

items.implementation_gap: Replace heuristic complexity-only routing with measured capacity, ISA compatibility, memory bounds and isolation requirements.
items.acceptance_test: An infeasible workload is queued or refused; placement never violates a hard resource or ISA constraint.

items.implementation_gap: Implement priority, starvation prevention, backpressure and queue-capacity limits with durable work identifiers.
items.acceptance_test: Overload produces bounded queues and explicit rejection while admitted tenants receive the chosen fairness guarantee.

items.implementation_gap: Continuously reconcile desired state to observed instances through generation-scoped idempotent operations.
items.acceptance_test: Restarting the controller or redelivering a command neither duplicates instances nor loses an admitted workload.

items.implementation_gap: Separate successful build, boot, ready service, live process, completed invocation and correct application output.
items.acceptance_test: A booted but incorrect or stalled guest is not marked ready; probes have deadlines and output-size limits.

items.implementation_gap: Stop admission, drain accepted work, flush state within a bound, then terminate and preserve a definitive exit reason.
items.acceptance_test: Stop during active I/O either commits or records an interrupted operation without silently reporting completion.

items.component: Safe restart and failure budget policy
items.implementation_gap: Define retryable versus permanent failures, exponential backoff, restart ceilings and quarantine for deterministic crashes.
items.acceptance_test: A crash loop cannot consume unbounded resources or repeatedly promote a known-bad image.

items.implementation_gap: Add explicit stateless/stateful scaling semantics, allocation reservations and drain-before-replace behavior.
items.acceptance_test: Scaling out or in respects application state semantics and does not lose accepted requests or bypass quotas.

items.implementation_gap: Provide versioned structured operations and errors; keep CLI presentation separate from machine contracts and long-running job IDs.
items.acceptance_test: Contract tests exercise command/API parity and incompatible-version refusal without parsing human log text.

items.implementation_gap: Authenticate local broker clients and any remote control endpoints; design offline identity provisioning first.
items.acceptance_test: Unauthenticated and expired identities cannot load, seal, mount, read secrets or stop another workload.

items.implementation_gap: Define distinct permissions for read, build, execute, seal, sign, trust enrollment and destructive lifecycle actions.
items.acceptance_test: A read-only operator cannot escalate through an indirect command or optional argument.

items.implementation_gap: Separate state roots, credentials, image references, quotas and backend instances by tenant identity.
items.acceptance_test: Cross-tenant name collisions, aliases and shared-cache references cannot expose mutable data.

items.implementation_gap: Evaluate signed provenance, runtime class, resource budgets, device access and network requirements before any executable action.
items.acceptance_test: A denied policy leaves no child process or externally visible partial workload; policy evidence is recorded.

items.implementation_gap: Specify configuration schemas, precedence, secret references, defaults and generation-aware updates; reject unknown sensitive fields.
items.acceptance_test: Invalid configuration is rejected atomically and an attempted downgrade cannot weaken an existing workload policy.

items.implementation_gap: Keep secrets out of cargo, TIFFs, manifests, process arguments and public logs; supply scoped short-lived handles at runtime.
items.acceptance_test: A redaction test finds no test secret in emitted artifacts, logs, snapshots or another tenant's state.

items.implementation_gap: Record actor, command, policy decision, generation and outcome in an append-only independently anchored audit stream.
items.acceptance_test: Changing or removing a recorded sensitive operation is detectable without trusting the same mutable workspace.

items.implementation_gap: Extend staging/journals to berth, bill of lading, ship seals, hull mounts and runtime state with explicit commit/recovery semantics.
items.acceptance_test: Crash injection at every mutation step recovers a coherent old or new generation with no missing cargo.

items.implementation_gap: Turn the 512-page stop guard into validated immutable checkpoints, bounded history segments and an explicit restore index.
items.acceptance_test: Long-running TIFF state continues after rollover and restores the same state as uninterrupted execution.

items.implementation_gap: Commit all participating node, fabric and hull results under one epoch or persist an explicit partial-tick record and recovery plan.
items.acceptance_test: Power-loss simulation between any two picture writes never leaves an apparently complete mixed-generation tick.

items.component: Strict state schema and decoder boundary
items.implementation_gap: Apply bounded schema validation to every TIFF/JSON/blob entry point, including embedded hull decoders, previews and import paths.
items.acceptance_test: Malformed metadata, dimensions, integer fields and nested structures are rejected inside a bounded decoder worker.

items.implementation_gap: Reserve space for staging, image growth and backups before mutation; enforce minimum free-space thresholds and aggregate quotas.
items.acceptance_test: A low-disk fault stops before destructive commit and preserves a usable recovery copy and clear error record.

items.implementation_gap: Track references from active generations, snapshots and retained backups; quarantine then remove only unreferenced artifacts.
items.acceptance_test: A concurrent deployment/restore cannot lose a referenced object; dry-run lists exactly the reclaimable bytes.

items.implementation_gap: Define snapshot format, engine/ABI compatibility, encrypted secret handling and schema migration with validation before restore.
items.acceptance_test: A snapshot restored on a supported clean host resumes with equivalent application state; incompatible ABI is refused.

items.implementation_gap: Provide operator-facing inspect, restore and abandon commands for retained backups and transaction journals, with generation checks.
items.acceptance_test: Automated restore returns registry, seals and mount state to a verified generation rather than only moving a directory.

items.implementation_gap: Define request/response buffers, handles, errors and ownership across the actual guest boundary; default to local transport.
items.acceptance_test: Unknown operations, invalid handles and out-of-bounds buffers cannot reach arbitrary host functions.

items.implementation_gap: Specify maximum lengths, canonical field encodings, numeric bounds, checksums and compatibility handling for every frame.
items.acceptance_test: Truncated, oversized, duplicate-field and mismatched-version messages are rejected without desynchronizing the channel.

items.implementation_gap: Use bounded queues, byte budgets, flow control and nonblocking cancellation instead of unbounded message accumulation.
items.acceptance_test: Producer floods remain within a measured buffer budget and cannot deadlock unrelated workloads.

items.implementation_gap: Assign request IDs and epochs; state at-most-once/at-least-once behavior and deduplicate side effects where needed.
items.acceptance_test: Repeated or out-of-order messages cannot double-apply a committed external effect or overwrite newer state.

items.implementation_gap: Carry deadlines across scheduler, guest IPC and storage operations using suitable monotonic clocks.
items.acceptance_test: Canceled work stops using resources within its specified bound and has a deterministic final disposition.

items.implementation_gap: Where zero-copy is selected, validate grant lifetime, size, direction and revocation; otherwise keep bounded copied buffers.
items.acceptance_test: Revoked or cross-tenant grants cannot be used after stop, replacement or channel reset.

items.implementation_gap: For networked workloads only, add the selected virtual NIC, IP stack, TLS, DNS behavior and explicitly granted ingress/egress policy.
items.acceptance_test: The offline profile still has no network access; approved endpoints work and all other routes remain denied.

items.implementation_gap: For multi-service deployments, publish authenticated generation-aware endpoints with readiness, expiry and withdrawal.
items.acceptance_test: A stopped or replaced generation cannot receive newly routed requests after its endpoint is withdrawn.

items.implementation_gap: Separate development, build, release and operator trust keys; support rotation, revocation, offline roots and scoped enrollment.
items.acceptance_test: A revoked signer cannot admit new images; one compromised online role cannot mint a new trusted root.

items.implementation_gap: Use authenticated versioned update metadata and a trustworthy expiry/version policy suitable for offline distribution.
items.acceptance_test: Older, expired or inconsistent metadata cannot silently replace a newer approved release.

items.implementation_gap: Verify cached engine source, libraries and executables against the approved dependency graph immediately before use; protect mutable roots.
items.acceptance_test: Changing a cached adapter or native executable blocks execution even when the original hold ZIP still matches its pin.

items.implementation_gap: Bind state to exact image, ABI, configuration, policy, tenant and generation instead of a name or accumulator alone.
items.acceptance_test: State replay from a different image or tenant is rejected before guest execution.

items.implementation_gap: Label byte integrity, signature authenticity, witness agreement, semantic correctness and isolation evidence separately.
items.acceptance_test: No promotion rule treats a deterministic hash witness as proof of arbitrary program correctness or authority.

items.implementation_gap: Review and fuzz the actual C engines, image loaders, device handlers and interpreters with sanitizers and hardened builds.
items.acceptance_test: Adversarial image/bytecode corpora complete without sanitizer findings; each remaining finding has an explicit blocker.

items.implementation_gap: Exercise host boundary attacks and document the chosen hardware/shared-resource threat model rather than asserting absolute isolation.
items.acceptance_test: Independent tests and host configuration evidence support the declared tenant boundary; unsupported threats are clearly excluded.

items.implementation_gap: Maintain reviewed component inventories, update policy, affected-image discovery and a revocation/rebuild workflow.
items.acceptance_test: A simulated vulnerable dependency can be located, blocked, rebuilt and rolled back without disabling unrelated workloads.

items.implementation_gap: Bound stdout, stderr, event logs and retained audit records; classify data and redact secrets at emission.
items.acceptance_test: Log floods do not exhaust memory/disk and a bounded final failure record remains available.

items.implementation_gap: Measure actual boot, queue, execution, memory, I/O and storage costs per image/generation with bounded label cardinality.
items.acceptance_test: Metrics reconcile with host observations and distinguish guest work from compiler, decoder and controller overhead.

items.implementation_gap: Correlate source/admission/build/boot/invocation/state commit IDs with bounded trace retention.
items.acceptance_test: One failed invocation can be traced to exact image, input generation, backend and commit disposition.

items.implementation_gap: Present boot/readiness/liveness/evidence status separately with last-progress age, current phase and actual blocked reason.
items.acceptance_test: A stale or stopped workload cannot continue showing healthy merely because its last witness passed.

items.implementation_gap: Report disk, memory, queue and history-limit pressure before admission or state advancement runs out of capacity.
items.acceptance_test: Controlled resource pressure triggers a visible actionable warning and preserves the stop/refusal policy.

items.implementation_gap: Retain source maps and bounded deterministic inputs for guest stepping and reproduction; distinguish simulation from real-time I/O.
items.acceptance_test: A recorded deterministic failure reproduces with the same observable state and flags unrecorded nondeterminism.

items.component: Crash dumps and support bundle export
items.implementation_gap: Export versioned redacted state, logs, hashes and host capability evidence without keys, user cargo leakage or unbounded archives.
items.acceptance_test: A support bundle is sufficient to reproduce a seeded failure and passes secret/content-scope checks.

items.component: Operator UI with explicit authority cues
items.implementation_gap: Build a small management view over the stable API: inspect, stage, run, stop, recover and review evidence; retain CLI parity.
items.acceptance_test: Destructive controls show scope and generation; UI status is derived from observed facts rather than animation or file presence.

items.implementation_gap: Only for multi-host scope: provision unique worker identities, enrollment policy and revocation independent of display names.
items.acceptance_test: Unknown/revoked workers cannot receive cargo, join scheduling or publish trusted results.

items.implementation_gap: Add authenticated encrypted bounded RPC and explicit cross-machine authorization; the offline profile must stay blocked.
items.acceptance_test: A remote endpoint cannot impersonate a worker or deliver oversized/replayed control messages.

items.implementation_gap: Choose and specify a real consensus protocol and failure model for desired state; local ALLREDUCE witness agreement is not consensus.
items.acceptance_test: Leader loss and network partition preserve the specified single-writer safety and recovery/liveness assumptions.

items.implementation_gap: Use epochs/fencing tokens to prevent old workers from committing after ownership moves or leases expire.
items.acceptance_test: An isolated previous owner cannot mutate committed state after a new owner is activated.

items.implementation_gap: Model independent hosts/zones and partial connectivity; avoid treating four interpreters on one host as four fault domains.
items.acceptance_test: Loss of one selected fault domain preserves the explicitly promised replicas and never double-commits state.

items.implementation_gap: Replicate immutable objects with digest validation and define consistency and placement rules for mutable state.
items.acceptance_test: A worker resumes from independently verified objects after source-host loss; corrupt replicas are rejected.

items.implementation_gap: Support mixed worker/image/ABI versions during controlled rollouts with admission and rollback gates.
items.acceptance_test: Canary failure stops the rollout; incompatible state or protocol versions never silently interoperate.

items.implementation_gap: Test full controller/worker loss, restored identity and data, split brain and lost update metadata in the declared topology.
items.acceptance_test: A documented drill meets chosen recovery objectives without trusting stale leaders or unsigned replacement artifacts.

items.implementation_gap: Run native Windows, Linux and any claimed macOS environments, including spaces, long roots, NTFS reparse points and no-toolchain hosts.
items.acceptance_test: Every supported platform has machine-recorded launch/build/verify results; simulated path checks do not count as OS execution.

items.implementation_gap: Fuzz archive, manifest, image, TIFF, bytecode and IPC parsers inside resource-limited workers with a retained corpus.
items.acceptance_test: A budgeted campaign has reproducible seeds and no unexplained crashes, hangs, overreads or unbounded allocations.

items.implementation_gap: Extend example regressions to generated legal/illegal lifecycle sequences, alias invariants and arithmetic edge cases.
items.acceptance_test: Generated transitions preserve ownership, byte conservation, integrity and monotonic generation properties.

items.component: Crash, disk-full and concurrency fault injection
items.implementation_gap: Inject process termination, partial writes, ENOSPC, permission changes and competing operators at every commit boundary.
items.acceptance_test: Recovery converges to a documented state without data loss or a false successful verdict across repeated trials.

items.implementation_gap: Benchmark boot, workload throughput, tail latency, peak RSS and long-run TIFF/checkpoint growth against explicit baselines.
items.acceptance_test: Published measurements include hardware, toolchain, sample count and failure rates; no estimated speedup is presented as measured.

items.implementation_gap: When OCI compatibility is selected, map guest images and lifecycle to specific pinned specification versions rather than merely adopting container names.
items.acceptance_test: OCI descriptors and chosen lifecycle contracts pass their conformance checks; unsupported OCI features are explicitly refused.

items.implementation_gap: Package short-path launchers, dependency checks, rollback and signed update metadata without silently overwriting user state.
items.acceptance_test: A clean install and interrupted upgrade on each supported OS preserve user cargo and restore an approved release.

items.implementation_gap: Define mandatory, optional and not-applicable gates; publish test scope, failures, residual risks and operator recovery procedures.
items.acceptance_test: No release is labeled operational or isolated while a required gate is skipped, untested or supported only by a declaration.

S1.title: Unikraft architecture
S1.basis: Modular library-OS APIs, selected platform targets and linked guest binaries.

S2.title: MirageOS
S2.basis: Standalone specialized guest images and library-OS runtime integration.

S3.title: Solo5 execution environment
S3.basis: Guest-facing ABI, host-facing tenders and isolation boundaries.

S4.title: Firecracker production host setup
S4.basis: Hardware isolation plus host-side privileges, syscall, network and resource policies.

S5.title: OCI image specification
S5.basis: Content-addressed descriptors, image metadata and interoperable packaging.

S6.title: OCI runtime specification
S6.basis: Runtime lifecycle and configuration contracts; interoperability is optional here.

S7.title: SLSA v1.2
S7.basis: Build/source assurance tracks and independently verifiable provenance.

S8.title: The Update Framework specification
S8.basis: Trusted update metadata, role separation, version/expiration and rollback defenses.
